subject: Request: Confirmation of data exposure status after 2027-04-11 incident
messages:
From: Diane Clark <diane.clark@helium-payments.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: security@helium-payments.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Incident - request for quick confirmation on data exposure

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the initial status update this morning. Helium's security team needs a succinct confirmation for our internal stakeholders: did the incident you described result in any access to or exfiltration of customer data (payment tokens, transactions, PII)? Specifically, we need:

- A one-line statement we can include in our internal brief (yes/no/no evidence found).
- A brief description of the checks you ran (logs, storage scan, KV cache).
- Any supporting artifacts you can share (sample logs, hash reconciliation summary).

We appreciate an answer within 48 hours if possible — our execs are consolidating an update. If there are follow-up questions or you'd prefer a short call, we can make time.

Best,
Diane
Diane Clark
Head of Security Operations
Helium Payments

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Incident - request for quick confirmation on data exposure

Team — forwarding Helium's ask. They need a crisp "no evidence of customer data access" statement plus evidence artifacts. Action items: 

- Monica: run the log sampling and produce a short hash reconciliation (S3/object store + request logs + KV cache). Prioritize requests that map to Helium account IDs.
- Markus: confirm whether any ephemeral inference workers had mounted persistent volumes or accessed S3 buckets during the window (2027-04-11 08:40 - 09:30 UTC).
- Mina: collect the audit trail from KMS access logs and the tenant routing records.

Can we have an internal summary for me by EOD tomorrow so I can send Helium a reply? If anything looks suspicious, escalate immediately and loop in legal/CS.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Incident - request for quick confirmation on data exposure

Sofia/Markus/Mina,

Quick forensic summary (high level) — full notes attached. I ran the following checks across the incident window (2027-04-11 08:40 - 09:30 UTC):

1) Request-level logs: sampled 10k requests across affected frontends. All request payloads show normal routing headers; no requests contained customer data patterns outside expected API inputs.

2) Object storage (S3) access logs: looked for reads/writes originating from the implicated container instances. No GetObject/PutObject events from those instances in the window.

3) KV cache (in-memory): audited cache operations for keys tagged to Helium account IDs; cache eviction and access counts were within normal patterns; no exports or snapshot operations were triggered.

4) KMS/audit logs: no Decrypt/GenerateDataKey operations attributable to anomalous principals.

5) Binary/exfiltration checks: outbound network flows from the infected host were limited to internal services; there were no large multipart uploads or unusual external connections during the period.

6) Hash reconciliation: we computed SHA256 hashes for a sampled set of persisted objects and compared against the expected inventory. Attached file "20270413_hash-summary.txt" contains the reconciled list (all hashes matched).

Conclusion (preliminary): No evidence of customer data access or exfiltration based on log sampling, S3 access records, KV cache audit, and hash reconciliation. I have attached a CSV sample of the request logs we used and the hash summary.

Attachments: 20270413_hash-summary.txt, 20270413_log-sample.csv, forensic-checklist-helion.pdf

If you'd like, we can expand the sample size or run a full object-store reconciliation — estimate 48 more hours for a full deterministic sweep.

- Monica
Principal Incident Responder
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Diane Clark <diane.clark@helium-payments.com>
Cc: security@helium-payments.com
Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Incident - request for quick confirmation on data exposure

Diane —

Thanks for your patience while we completed the initial forensic checks. Summary for your internal briefing below (one-line + short evidence summary). Please treat the attachments as evidence artifacts for your audit.

One-line statement: "No evidence of customer data access or exfiltration detected in our initial forensic sweep covering 2027-04-11 08:40 - 09:30 UTC."

What we checked (summary):
- Request sampling: 10k requests sampled for Helium-related traffic; no anomalous payloads or unauthorized read attempts were observed.
- Object store (S3): no GetObject/PutObject events from implicated hosts; SHA256 reconciliation for sampled persisted objects matched inventory (see hash summary).
- KV cache audit: no snapshots/export operations; access patterns normal for the window.
- KMS/audit trail: no suspicious decrypt or key material access events.
- Network egress: no large external transfers or unknown destinations during the period.

Artifacts attached: 20270413_hash-summary.txt, 20270413_log-sample.csv, forensic-checklist-helion.pdf

Next steps/options:
- If you require a deterministic, full reconciliation of all persisted objects for Helium's tenant (not just sampling), we can schedule a deeper sweep — estimated 48 hours and we'll need a maintenance window to hold writes.
- We're happy to join a short call to walk through the artifacts and answer questions.

If you want the one-line summary in a particular wording for your internal deck, tell me how you'd like it phrased and I'll send an approved line you can paste in.

Best regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270413_hash-summary.txt (text), 20270413_log-sample.csv (csv), forensic-checklist-helion.pdf (pdf)
